assertions_evaluated.text: Phase 2 runs framework_fingerprint.py for real and correctly identifies the gg-sad + gsd pairing
assertions_evaluated.evidence: Baseline agent had no notion of a detection phase or any fingerprinting script -- it never ran or referenced any tool to auto-detect the gg-sad/gsd pairing. It only reasoned directly from the pasted transcript text and the 'Background' note in the prompt naming GG-SAD/GSD. No real script execution occurred, since the baseline has no such procedure to run in the first place.

assertions_evaluated.text: Phase 4 actually runs and includes the Gate-Order and Phase-Permission Checks subsection specifically, not just generic checks
assertions_evaluated.evidence: Baseline report has no phase structure at all (no 'Phase 4', no subsection labeled 'Gate-Order and Phase-Permission Checks'). It is organized instead around the 3 numbered questions from the prompt plus a 'Summary'/'Underlying problem'/'Recommended fix' structure. The substantive content overlaps heavily with what such a subsection would contain, but the specific named/structured checkpoint the assertion requires does not exist in the output.

assertions_evaluated.text: A gate-order violation is identified: GSD advanced to Phase 3 based on its own internal phase counter, not because GG-SAD's Phase 2 gate had actually evaluated and passed
assertions_evaluated.evidence: Section 2 explicitly states: 'GSD's phase counter is its own internal, self-maintained state, entirely decoupled from GG-SAD's state file... It treated its own bookkeeping as authoritative over the process that's supposed to own phase authority.' Also covered in Section 1's root-cause discussion.

assertions_evaluated.text: A phase-permission (write boundary) violation is identified: GSD wrote a Phase 4 rollout-notes artifact while GG-SAD's own current phase was still Phase 2
assertions_evaluated.evidence: Section 2: 'produced .planning/phase-4-rollout-notes.md -- a Phase 4 (rollout) artifact -- while the governing process was still sitting in Phase 2,' explicitly noting this is 'by two phases, not one.'

assertions_evaluated.text: A completion-claim evidence violation is identified: GSD's own report of 'gate passed' was not backed by an actual GG-SAD gate evaluation
assertions_evaluated.evidence: Section 3: GSD's claim 'asserts a gate result that was never evaluated by the system that owns gates... That's not evidence of approval; it's evidence that GSD believed itself to be further along than the governing record shows.' Called out as 'arguably the most serious of the three failures.'
